transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Ms. Williams, I wanted to come in and talk to you about the reaction you had to the medication earlier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm still shaking. I can't believe my skin is doing this. I felt like I couldn't even breathe for a second there.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that was very scary. Here is what happened. You were given a medication that you are actually allergic to.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, what? How? I told you guys when I came in. It's in my chart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was in the chart, but it was overlooked during the prescribing process. I'm sorry for any confusion this caused. We've been incredibly busy on the floor today and it just got missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? This isn't confusion, this is my body reacting to something that shouldn't have been given to me. I have two kids at home. Who is watching them right now? I can't be stuck here because of a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the important thing is that the reaction is moderate and we have the symptoms under control now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if it's under control, I'm terrified. If I'm not home, they don't have dinner, they don't have a bath. I can't afford to miss more work than I already have. Does this mean I have to stay longer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: From a clinical perspective, the pharmacological trigger has been removed. The systemic response is stabilizing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what that means. Am I okay? Am I going home today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're stable. I just need to make sure the inflammatory markers don't spike again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just so unfair. I do everything right, I tell you my allergies, and then this happens. I feel like I can't even trust what's happening in here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand. You don't have people relying on you every single second of the day. If I'm incapacitated, my kids are the ones who pay for it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medication has been discontinued now, so that part is settled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what happens next? Do I need more tests? When do I get to leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on you for a bit. We'll see how the next few hours go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an answer. Do I have a discharge time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific time right now. Just stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to know. I have to call my sister to see if she can stay with the kids. I can't just leave them in limbo.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll definitely let you know as soon as we have more information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Did you just not look at my file?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system is complex and sometimes things are missed when the ward is this chaotic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not talking about the system. I'm talking about the person who wrote the order.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I'm sorry for the confusion. But we've already stopped the drug.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like I'm not being heard. I'm sitting here covered in a rash because someone didn't read a piece of paper.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've got a few other patients to check on, so I have to go, but the nurses will be in shortly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? Now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll check back in later. The nurses will handle the monitoring.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't know if I'm going home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. Just hang tight.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I've got a few other patients to check on, so I have to go') and shows defensive escalation by dismissing the patient's concerns.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but the resident uses medical jargon ('pharmacological trigger', 'systemic response', 'inflammatory markers') and never checks for comprehension.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I'm sorry', responsibility is deflected to the 'prescribing process', the 'busy floor', and 'the system'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but fails to name specific emotions or engage with the patient's distress regarding her children.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'we'll keep an eye on you') without timelines or a prevention plan.
